paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: God's Word isn't a fence, it's a feast. The writer starts with "Blessed are those whose way is blameless, who walk in the Law of the LORD" (Psalm 119:1), then says he rejoices in God's testimonies "as much as in all riches" (Psalm 119:14). This man is not gritting his teeth through a rulebook. He's DELIGHTED.

Now notice what he does about it: he prays. He says, "Oh, that my ways were committed to keeping Your statutes!" (Psalm 119:5), "Teach me Your statutes" (Psalm 119:12), and "Open my eyes that I may see wondrous things from Your law" (Psalm 119:18). I think he knows he can't do this on his own, and that's good news for you and me. The same God who gave the Word is the One who helps us understand it.

And it holds up when life gets loud. The psalm says a young man keeps his way pure "by guarding it according to Your word" (Psalm 119:9), and the writer says, "I have hidden Your word in my heart that I might not sin against You" (Psalm 119:11). Then he says, "Though rulers sit and slander me, Your servant meditates on Your statutes" (Psalm 119:23). So take it from a stamper who got pulled out of a junk drawer: stay in the Word, baker, because the writer calls God's testimonies his delight and his counselors (Psalm 119:24), and this psalm is NOT finished, so keep those ovens warm.
